depends_on: Landau's theorem on sums of two squares (or Dirichlet's theorem for primes 3 mod 4)
category_override: answered elsewhere; confirmed or written up here
notes: a(n) = sum of (-1)^k over (6k-1)^2 + 9(2j+1)^2 = 24n + 10, so a(n) != 0 forces 24n + 10 to be a sum of two squares; Landau gives #{n < N : a(n) != 0} = O(N/sqrt(log N)), density of zeros 1. Instance of Serre's 1976 lacunarity of weight-1 forms. Outside Lean: everything (pentagonal theorem, Landau or Dirichlet); identity checked numerically to n = 20000.

sources: J.-P. Serre, Divisibilite de certaines fonctions arithmetiques, Enseignement Math. 22 (1976)
prior_art.note: Follows from Serre's theorem for weight-1 forms; explicit two-squares argument written here.
